v0: Find Your Stress Source: The 7-Day Body Log
v2: When your body is tense all the time, the cause is often hidden. Track your body and your days for a week to find the pattern.
v3: Three times a day, rate your body tension from 0 to 10 and note where you feel it (jaw, shoulders, chest, stomach)
v4: Write what happened in the hour before: people, tasks, news, screens, food, caffeine
v5: Each night, note your sleep, any worries you carried, and anything left unfinished
v6: After seven days, circle the times tension was highest and what they have in common
v7: Choose one cause to work on first, and tell someone safe what you found
v8: I am tense all the time, there is no pattern

v11: Set three phone reminders, or log at meals
v12: The log makes me more anxious

v14: A body stuck in stress mode is usually responding to something: an ongoing threat, an unfinished stress cycle, poor recovery or a physical cause. Logging brings hidden patterns into awareness, which engages the prefrontal cortex and gives you a clear target instead of vague dread.
v15: If your body always feels tight or worried, write down how you feel and what happened, a few times a day for a week. Then you can see what is making you stressed.
v18: Dealing with the cause of stress is not the same as dealing with the stress itself. Your body needs a signal that the danger is over.
v19: Move your body until you breathe harder: a brisk walk, dancing, cycling or climbing stairs
v20: Then do one calming signal: a long hug of 20 seconds, a good cry, deep laughter or slow breathing
v21: Notice your body settle: shoulders drop, breath slows
v22: Thank God that you are safe right now
v23: Do this on stressful days, even when the problem is not solved yet
v25: Ten minutes of brisk movement still helps

v29: Tears are part of how God designed the body to release stress
v30: Stress hormones prepare the body to act. When we sit still with them, they keep circulating. Movement uses them up, and signals like hugging, laughter and slow breathing tell the nervous system the threat has passed, so it can return to rest and digest.
v31: When you are stressed, your body needs to move and then rest. Walk fast or dance, then breathe slowly or have a hug. That tells your body, "The danger is over."
v34: A racing heart, constant fatigue or tension can come from the body itself, not only from stress. Get the simple checks done.
v35: List your physical symptoms and how long you have had them

v37: Check your intake of caffeine, energy drinks, nicotine and alcohol
v38: Take your results seriously and follow the treatment plan

v46: An overactive thyroid, anaemia, low blood sugar, stimulants and poor sleep all produce the same feelings as anxiety: a fast heart, shakiness, tension and tiredness. Treating a physical cause can calm the whole system.
v47: Sometimes the body feels stressed because something in the body needs a doctor. Get checked, and keep doing your calm habits too.

v96: Why the Body Stays in Stress Mode
